newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car sector says no euphoria for October data.
newsitem.headline: Italy car sector says no euphoria for October data.

text.p: Italian new car registrations data for October will be positive after heavy falls in September but industry sources said comparisons with October 1995 should take into account a "disastrous" month last year.
Italy's Transport Ministry is due to publish new car registration figures for October on Saturday.
Italian September new car registrations fell 8.55 percent to 116,000 units, the worst September data for 12 years.
The sources said the October data should show two-digit year-on-year growth to above 130,000 units against 118,000 in October last year.
But one source noted that in October 1995 sales were down a massive 10.32 percent because of a strike by drivers of car transporter trucks.
"The October data will be positive from a numerical point of view. There will be growth of quite a few percentage points," said another industry source who declined to be named.
"But there is a need for caution. October 1995 was a disastrous month, the worst month of the year, and there was also one less working day in the month compared to October this year," he added.
"I certainly don't think you can talk of a recovering market. October will be flat comparatively. But the fact that there won't be another fall is positive," another source said.
